Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve intent and certainty. Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "Budget records update for 2025

I’m sharing an update on the household budget records for 2025. The folder now contains the monthly summaries from January through October, the current bill calendar, and copies of the receipts that have been entered so far. November and December are still open months, so their totals are not included in the year-to-date figures. The records are for tracking income and spending; they do not replace statements from the bank, utility companies, or other providers.

The working spreadsheet is named “Household Budget 2025” and is saved in the shared folder under Finance > Budget Records. The printed copy is in the blue binder on the lower shelf beside the desk. The spreadsheet has separate tabs for monthly totals, recurring bills, irregular expenses, and savings transfers. The binder has the same sections, with receipts filed behind the month in which each purchase was made. A dated note on the binder’s front pocket lists the last time the paper copy was updated.

For consistency, the records use the date a transaction posted to the account, rather than the date on which a purchase was made. When those dates differ, the receipt date is kept in the notes column. For example, the October 31 grocery purchase posted on November 1; it appears in October’s spending total, with both dates noted. Refunds are entered as credits in the category associated with the original purchase. The spreadsheet’s category names have not changed since the start of the year, which allows the monthly figures to be compared on the same basis.

1. **What is included:** The monthly summaries show recorded income, routine household costs, flexible spending, and transfers to savings. The “Home” category includes rent, electricity, water, and the internet bill. Groceries and household supplies are listed separately, even when they appear on the same store receipt. Medical expenses are recorded at the amount paid, while reimbursements are entered separately when they appear in the account.
2. **What is not included:** The summaries do not estimate cash purchases for which no note or receipt was kept. They also do not include credit-card charges that have not yet posted, pending refunds, or bills dated after October 31. These items may be added when their amounts and dates are available. A blank cell means that no amount has been entered; it does not mean that the expense was zero.
3. **How to submit a receipt:** Place paper receipts in the envelope marked “To enter” in the desk drawer, or send a clear photograph to the shared budget folder. Include the purchase date and a short note if the receipt covers more than one category. For a receipt with both groceries and cleaning products, for instance, the note can give the amount assigned to each. Please do not write account numbers or full card details on a receipt before filing it.
4. **How corrections are recorded:** If an entry appears to be wrong, add a comment to the spreadsheet cell or leave a note in the binder. Include the month, amount, and merchant when those details are known. The original entry will remain visible in the spreadsheet’s change history, and the corrected amount will be entered with a brief explanation. This keeps the record of what changed without relying on a separate message thread.

The recurring-bills tab lists the usual due date and the amount recorded for each bill. Some amounts vary from month to month, so the figure shown is the posted charge, not a forecast. The electricity bill, for example, was $84.16 in August and $96.42 in September. The internet charge remained $58.00 in both months. The calendar also marks the annual renter’s insurance payment in March and the vehicle registration payment in July. Those entries identify the months in which the charges appeared; they do not indicate that the same amounts will apply next year.

The savings section records transfers from the checking account to the emergency fund. It currently shows transfers of $75 in February, $100 in April, and $50 in August. These are listed as transfers rather than household expenses so they are not counted again as spending. The account balance itself is not copied into the budget spreadsheet. Anyone checking a balance or confirming a transfer should use the account’s own statement or online records.

The October summary was updated on November 6. It includes transactions posted through October 31 and receipts received by that date. Three grocery receipts from October are still in the “To enter” envelope, and one pharmacy receipt is missing its purchase date. They are not included in the current totals. If the dates or amounts become clear, the entries can be added to the October tab with a note showing when the information was received. The next routine review is scheduled for December 5, when the November records will be checked against the available account activity.

As Maya put it when we reviewed the folder, “It helps to have the paper copy and the spreadsheet tell the same story.” The binder and spreadsheet are both available for reference, and either one can be used to flag a missing receipt or question about an entry. This update describes the records currently on file; it does not provide a final total for 2025, since November and December have not been closed.", "output": "Budget records update for 2025

Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "i'm trying to get my personal budget records into a shape where i can actually compare one month with another, and i wondered if you might be willing to look over the folders with me. i don't need you to decide what i should spend or to tell me whether a purchase was sensible. what would help is a careful second set of eyes on the way i've recorded things, especially where the same kind of expense appears under different names. i want to keep the original statements and receipts as they are, so i'm asking for help organizing my notes, not changing anything from the bank or card companies.

the records cover january through june this year. there are checking-account statements for all six months, card statements for february through june, and a small envelope of cash receipts from march and april. i also have a spreadsheet that i started in january, but i didn't enter everything in it at the same time. some entries were added from the statement later, and a few cash purchases were written down from memory a day or two after they happened. i think the dates are right, though i can't promise that for every cash item. i would rather mark those as uncertain than have us guess a date just to make the rows look complete.

could you help me check these parts, if you have time?
1. compare the spreadsheet totals with the statement totals for each month, without assuming that a difference means one of the records is wrong. in april, for example, the spreadsheet is $18.40 lower than the checking statement, but that might be because i left out the annual library fee or entered it somewhere else. i haven't found it yet. in may, a $42.00 payment is shown on the card statement as “Northside Market,” while my note says groceries. i believe it was groceries, but i don't remember what was bought, and i don't want the description on the statement replaced.
2. look for repeated charges and transfers that could be counted twice. the rent is listed as “Oak Court rent” in the spreadsheet and “ACH payment” on the checking statement, and the amount is $1,275 each month. i think those are the same payment, but please flag any month where the date or amount doesn't line up. the $65.00 transfer from checking to savings on the 12th is not an expense, even though i accidentally put it in my first draft of the monthly spending total. i'd like that noted rather than quietly deleted from the old version.
3. help me group the expense labels in a consistent way. i have used “home,” “household,” and “supplies” for purchases from the hardware store, and i can't remember whether all of them were for the apartment. please don't decide that they all belong together if the notes don't say that. a short list of entries that need my attention would be more useful than a confident category based on the store name alone.

one tricky group is the card charges from Greenline Pharmacy. the February entry is $16.28 and the March one is $31.06; the notes for both just say “pharmacy.” the March receipt is in the envelope, folded behind a grocery receipt, but i haven't checked what it was for. there is also a $9.50 cash entry in April labeled “medicine?” with a question mark. i'm not certain whether that was medicine or another small purchase, so please leave the question mark in place unless the receipt settles it. i don't want the pharmacy name to be treated as proof of what each charge contained.

i have separate tabs for groceries and eating out, but i wasn't consistent about them. a few cafe purchases are under groceries because i bought bread or coffee beans at the same time, and two grocery-store visits include a ready-made meal. i'd like you to point out entries that look ambiguous, not move them based on a rule we invent while looking at the sheet. the note “lunch with Jo” appears beside a $14.75 charge in March, and “team lunch” appears beside $22.10 in May. those notes are all i have; i don't know whether either should be treated as work-related, and i don't want to infer that from the wording.

please keep the original wording of descriptions such as “Northside Market,” “Oak Court rent,” and “team lunch,” even if you add a separate suggested category beside them. if you suggest a change, could you make it in a new column or in a copy of the spreadsheet, so the first version is still there to compare? for unclear entries, a note like “check receipt” or “not sure” is fine. if the receipt is missing, just flag that rather than filling in a likely explanation. i may be able to remember a few details when i see the list, but i don't want you to have to make those decisions for me.

i'm hoping we can go through the records in about an hour, but we don't have to finish every month in one sitting. the most useful first step would be checking the monthly totals and making a separate list of anything that doesn't match or needs my memory. after that, if it still seems manageable, we could look at the category names. would you be comfortable helping me with that, and telling me if any part of the spreadsheet is too messy to check quickly?", "output": "I'm trying to get my personal budget records into a shape where I can actually compare one month with another, and I wondered if you might be willing to look over the folders with me. one morning, our usual room was being used, so we sat near the front windows instead. it was noisier there, and i worried the children wouldn't settle, but they seemed to like watching people come and go. a father who had barely spoken during earlier sessions read a book about a small boat. he paused to let his daughter finish the repeated line, and she was so pleased that she wanted to read it again. i still think about that moment. the sessions were simple, and not every morning went smoothly, but sharing the reading made the library feel more welcoming to me.", "output": "For most of last winter, I ran a reading hour for parents and young children at the branch library on Thursday mornings.
